purpose: Split the 63% star-particle section into work vs synchronization

result.conclusion: SPFinalize == SPCommUpdateCount to 0.1 s: the ENTIRE cost of StarParticleFinalize is the single MPI_Allreduce in CommunicationUpdateStarParticleCount. StarParticleInitialize is negligible (0.3%) - the earlier suspicion that the FindTotalNumberOfParticles hierarchy walk was expensive is falsified (3.5 s).
result.payload: 2*NumberOfGrids ints (~1-8 kB) among 128 ranks ON A SINGLE NODE (shared-memory MPI): true payload cost is tens of microseconds. So ~100% of the 320 ms/call is synchronization wait, not communication.

imbalance_character.interpretation: No rank sits near zero at the barrier, so there is no single persistently-slow rank absorbing the work while others wait. The slowest rank VARIES between subcycles - the imbalance fluctuates. That is the regime where removing unnecessary barriers pays: wall time is currently sum-over-subcycles of max-over-ranks, and without the barrier it tends toward max-over-ranks of the sum (max(sum) <= sum(max)).

opportunity.description: User observation (2026-07-30): FOGGIE sets StarFormationOncePerRootGridTimeStep=1, so SetMakeStars() runs only at level 0 once per root step (EvolveLevel.C:415-427) and each grid clears its flag after its first StarParticleHandler call. New star particles can therefore only appear in the FIRST subcycle of each level per root cycle - but the Allreduce runs on all 4327 subcycles. Its actual job (SetNewParticleIndex) is a no-op when nothing was created.
opportunity.prize: ~1388 s of 2214 s is barrier wait at this one call. Reducing 4327 collectives to ~55 (one per level per root cycle) could approach a 2x wall-clock improvement - larger than everything Tier 1 delivered combined (~7%).
risks: DEADLOCK: the skip condition must be identical on every rank without a collective. A local test ('did my grids make particles?') diverges. Note MakeStars itself diverges across ranks because Grid_StarParticleHandler returns on the processor check BEFORE clearing it.

STALE COUNTS: the Allreduce also refreshes non-owned grids' particle counts as a side effect; particles migrate between grids at rebuild (every 2 subcycles). Must confirm nothing between rebuilds depends on that refresh.

WAIT MIGRATION: removing a barrier does not remove imbalance; it can relocate to the next sync point. Bounded by how much the fluctuating imbalance averages out - the spread data says a lot, but only a bench proves it.
